source.title: CaRe-BN: Precise Moving Statistics for Stabilizing Spiking Neural Networks in Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Zi-Jie Xu; Xinyu Shi; Yi-Ting Dong; Zihan Huang; Zhao-Fei Yu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests batch-normalization methods in spiking neural networks for reinforcement learning. Its reported outcomes concern returns, BN-statistic accuracy, and variance, not the training classification error or other behaviors named by these claim versions.
record.gate_note: No results are rows for V1–V6: the paper does not test the listed classification-error, local-minima, depth/shortcut, initialization, learning-rate stability, or BN-versus-no-BN claims. Its BN ablations and accuracy-related statements concern CaRe-BN's mechanisms and RL returns; the batch-normalization references are cited background. The paper also reports Wasserstein distance and exploration-return comparisons, but these do not measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study uses BN to stabilize SNN reinforcement learning and evaluates its proposed BN-statistics estimator through policy returns, return variance and distribution-estimation accuracy. These outcomes do not measure V6's classification-accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance, and no results test V1–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that CaRe-BN improves BN-statistics estimation, stabilizes SNN reinforcement learning and improves control performance. The reported 5.9% advantage over ANN counterparts is an aggregate across five TD3 continuous-control tasks, rather than an advantage on every task.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes confidence-adaptive and recalibration batch normalization for spiking neural networks in reinforcement learning; it does not test the original methods or measures in the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: CaRe-BN improves SNN reinforcement-learning returns in many tested settings, with an aggregate gain up to 22.62% over vanilla SNNs (Tables 10–15). These comparisons evaluate the proposed normalization method using policy returns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More accurate moving BN statistics can improve learning and policy returns in directly trained spiking reinforcement-learning agents.

fits_no_version.finding: For shallow ANN reinforcement-learning agents, the authors report similar performance with and without CaRe-BN (Section 5.6; Figures 11–12). Aggregate maximum-return gains are 0.33% with DDPG and −0.69% with TD3 (Tables 18–19). Policy returns do not measure V6's classification accuracy or learning-rate tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding CaRe-BN provides little aggregate return improvement for the tested shallow ANN reinforcement-learning agents.

fits_no_version.finding: CaRe-BN reduces activation-distribution Wasserstein distance and improves exploration returns relative to conventional BN (Section 5.2, Figures 3–4). Neither measure establishes any listed claim version.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Improved inference-time BN-statistics estimation can improve exploration in online spiking reinforcement learning.

record.problems: Claim-relevant outcomes are not measured. Several reported RL comparisons are presented as smoothed figures rather than numerical tables; the text states seed counts and shaded uncertainty for these figures.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and effects of model size, regularization and training duration.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to the learning-rate stability threshold.
BN's effects on classification-accuracy learning curves and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup's normalization-free residual training.

record.verdict_notes: The empty result-row set is appropriate for V1–V6. References to unstable gradients and DDPG divergence do not test initialization effects or learning-rate stability thresholds.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration effects.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual network depth effects on classification training error; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Training dynamics above the stability limit, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence under different learning rates.
Whether BN accelerates accuracy gains or raises learning-rate tolerance on the specified ANN benchmarks, or whether Fixup allows residual networks to train without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Relies on BN's training benefits while comparing normalization strategies; does not test V6's classification-accuracy gains or higher-learning-rate tolerance.

tranche.reason: Uses normalization to stabilize SNN reinforcement learning and evaluates its proposed statistics estimator. Policy returns, return variance and estimation accuracy do not test the listed claim versions.

source_check.notes: No rows, statements or verdicts are listed. Section 5.6's negligible benefit in shallow ANN reinforcement learning does not challenge V6's specified classification settings.
